defects.title: Crash window protection not connected to production: StartInFlightDeliveryAsync only called on PrinterTransmissionUncertainException, no persistent InFlight record before send
defects.invariant: Print delivery crash-window protection requires a persistent InFlight record created BEFORE the physical printer transmission attempt, so that crashes between send and ack are recoverable
defects.mechanism: In KitchenPrintDispatchHostedService.cs ExecuteDeliveryAsync (lines 225-231), StartInFlightDeliveryAsync is ONLY called inside the catch block for PrinterTransmissionUncertainException - meaning the InFlight record is created AFTER the transmission attempt fails with uncertainty. There is no InFlight record created before transport.SendAsync at line 222. PhysicalPrintRecoveryService.StartInFlightDeliveryAsync (line 67) does create the record, but it's never called proactively before transmission. The crash window (between successful send and ack receipt) has no persistent record, so a Host crash in that window leaves the delivery state unknown with no recovery path.
defects.acceptance: Refactor ExecuteDeliveryAsync to call StartInFlightDeliveryAsync BEFORE transport.SendAsync, creating a persistent InFlight record with status InFlight. Then on success call ConfirmDeliverySuccessAsync; on PrinterTransmissionUncertainException call ReportCrashWindowUncertaintyAsync on the already-existing delivery. Add a test that simulates a crash between send and ack and verifies the delivery appears in GetPendingUnknownDeliveriesAsync for operator review.

limitations: The defect is confirmed by source code inspection. The call sequence in ExecuteDeliveryAsync clearly shows StartInFlightDeliveryAsync only in the catch block. The PhysicalPrintRecoveryService implementation supports pre-transmission InFlight creation (CreateInFlight at line 67) but it's not wired that way in the hosted service. No runtime test was executed - this is static code analysis only per the task constraints.
